{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a large fish outline, and the whole run was connected from the start (all 125 standing dominoes were in the fall path) when the push came. I laid the belly line, stroke 2, from the nose join along the underside to the low point of the belly. That stretch forms the lower half of the fish's body, which is a big part of what makes the shape read as a fish to the judge.

Execution: I started the belly as soon as the back line reached the nose, so the branch got the fall. I stopped at the agreed low point so the final stretch could carry on from there without overlap. After laying it I inspected the middle patch and the area near the head several times. Those checks confirmed the run was connected, and I left it alone rather than risk bumping anything. I kept my hands off for the final minutes.

Collaboration: I made sure no two of us were laying the same stroke. I confirmed the handoff point with Hana for the belly. I asked teammates to watch the nose join and the top line, and I shared what I found when I checked. I stayed away from the tail tip while it was being built.

Leadership: I helped coordinate who took which stroke, so builders didn't collide on shared ground. I raised the doubled bit near the head, got its origin clarified, and helped the table agree to leave it alone. I pushed for a hands-off discipline before the push, which protected a fully connected build.", "my_share_percent": 30}
